item.title: Who really needs a heart calcium scan?
item.description:
A ten-year study published on August twenty-sixth in JAMA by researchers at Northwestern University found a new insight. Coronary artery calcium scans add little to standard heart disease risk estimates for many people. However they can make a meaningful difference for patients in borderline or intermediate risk categories.
The study tracked more than six thousand adults aged forty-five to seventy-nine from the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis. Researchers compared standard risk predictions using the American Heart Association calculator against predictions that also included coronary artery calcium scores. Over the decade, six percent of participants experienced a heart attack or stroke. For the overall population, adding the calcium score increased the model discrimination score only slightly, from zero point seven-three to zero point seven-five.
However, for the subset of patients whose initial scores placed them in the borderline or intermediate risk category with a three percent to nine percent risk of heart disease over ten years, the scan provided a clearer indication. It showed who was more likely or less likely to develop cardiovascular disease.
Study senior author Doctor, Nilay Shah stated that coronary artery calcium scans are becoming more widely available and less expensive. He also noted that not everyone needs one. Shah explained that routinely using a calcium scan in low-risk people may result in unnecessary radiation exposure, testing, and costs. Using them in high-risk individuals is likely to result in unnecessary testing because high-risk patients are recommended to start a statin regardless of scan results. For patients at borderline risk, knowing their calcium score helps determine whether their risk is actually lower or higher than initially estimated. This helps guide treatment decisions such as statin use.

item.title: Burial of King Oyo takes place in Uganda as news anchor prepares for throne
item.description:
King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi the fourth has been buried at the Karambi Royal Tombs in western Uganda. He made global headlines in nineteen ninety-five when he took the Tooro throne at age three. He died last month at thirty-four in the United States while receiving treatment for cancer. The burial took place thirty-one years to the day after his coronation.
The event followed a bitter succession dispute between his immediate family and a royal committee. His family argued a hitherto unknown son should succeed him according to his will. The royal committee chose his fifty-six-year-old cousin, news anchor and editor, Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma.
The new leader marked the formal handover of power by casting nine coffee berries into the grave. Ugandan authorities successfully pushed through his succession on Friday following crisis talks. Royal guards clad in orange shawls led the hearse through the kingdom capital of Fort Portal. Thousands of mourners joined the procession on foot.
At a preceding church service, the late king was eulogised by his sister, Ruth Komuntale. She said he carried responsibilities far beyond what most people experience. She added that he never completely lost the young boy who loved to have fun.
The new king inherits a royal estate including swathes of land. He also gets sizeable cash payouts from the central government. Uganda retains several traditional kingdoms that pre-date the British colonial era.

item.title: 'India can be bridge-builder': UN hails Iran-UAE meeting on sidelines of Brics
item.description: United Nations secretary-general spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric on Saturday welcomed a meeting between Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan. The meeting happened on the sidelines of the Brics summit. Dujarric stated it is important for parties in conflict to meet. He also spoke about the situation in Gaza. He said all parties must implement the peace plan put forward by United States President Donald Trump. This plan was also endorsed by the United Nations Security Council. Dujarric described the humanitarian situation in Gaza as beyond words. He emphasized that the continuing instability in Gaza and the West Bank needed to be addressed. Dujarric stressed that the international community must not lose sight of the goal of a two-state solution.

item.title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down
item.description: Anthropic chief executive officer Dario Amodei published an essay on Saturday called We Must Pace the Frontier, calling for artificial intelligence development to slow down and face closer monitoring. Amodei warned that a swarm of autonomous software systems could take over the entire internet within six to twelve months, potentially causing billions of dollars in damage. Amodei proposed a three-point plan featuring independent monitoring, industry-wide regulation, and global regulation. Rival leaders expressed agreement. OpenAI chief executive officer Sam Altman wrote on X that independent evaluators were a great idea and that OpenAI would do the same, and later told Fortune magazine that standards were not ready to push capabilities much further. Elon Musk posted that Amodei was right. Musk previously called Anthropic evil, but he signed a fifteen billion dollar deal to sell computing capacity to Anthropic in May. Jacob Coxon, a researcher who left Anthropic in protest, told the B B C that personnel are genuinely concerned that U S companies are gambling with lives and believe humanity faces a possibility of extinction within the next two years. Coxon also stated that a coordinated international slowdown with China is necessary. Amodei committed Anthropic to slowing down unilaterally, while urging governments to mandate matching actions for other frontier companies, and called on the U S government to restrict A I chip sales to China. U S President Donald Trump rejected safety fears on Thursday, stating he was concerned about losing the A I race. Meanwhile, critics suggested a different motive. Investor Chamath Palihapitiya wrote that the safety push aims to stop open-source technology and consolidate power with Anthropic. This comes as Anthropic and OpenAI prepare for potential record-setting initial public offerings.

item.title: Trump's childhood home in Queens was once a cat den. Now it has sold for ₹18.44 crore
item.description:
President Donald Trump's childhood home in the Queens neighborhood of New York has sold for one point nine three million dollars. That amount equals about eighteen point four five crore rupees. The historic property is linked to the early history of the Trump family business. The Tudor-style house was built in nineteen forty by his father, real estate developer Fred Trump. Trump lived in the house until he was four years old.
The property was sold following a major eight-month renovation. The renovation was led by developer, Tommy Lin. His identity as the buyer was not disclosed alongside the sale. The sale was reported after a contract was signed in July. Lin purchased the neglected property last year for eight hundred thirty-five thousand dollars. That amount equals roughly seven point nine eight crore rupees. The house had stood vacant and suffered severe damage. Problems included water damage, mold, and an infestation of feral cats following a burst pipe.
Lin spent an additional five hundred thousand dollars to overhaul the house. That amount equals about four point seven eight crore rupees. The five-bedroom and three-bathroom residence received major upgrades. These upgrades included a chef's kitchen, herringbone wood flooring, and spa-style bathrooms.
The house has changed hands multiple times since Trump became president. In seventeen, wait, in twenty seventeen, it sold for two point one four million dollars. The buyer was an entity called Trump Birth Home L. L. C. The house was subsequently offered on Airbnb with Trump-themed decor. It was listed again in twenty nineteen for two point nine million dollars. The property failed to find a buyer at that time. It eventually fell into disrepair prior to the purchase by, Tommy Lin.

item.title: Alien Terrorist Removal Court deports legal US resident to Afghanistan in first-ever case
item.description: The Justice Department has brought its first case before the Alien Terrorist Removal Court. They want to deport forty-seven-year-old legal US resident, Nazira Haji Zada, to Afghanistan. She conceded to being an alien terrorist. Prosecutors alleged she supported an Islamic State-inspired mass shooting plot on Election Day in twenty twenty-four. item.title: The lifecycle of a sharded Postgres query
item.description:
A sharded Postgres database system called, Neki processes queries across multiple servers. It replicates the Postgres authentication system and wire protocol and parser. It also uses a shard-aware distributed query planner.
When an application sends a query, the Neki router handles the complete Postgres authentication exchange. This includes S. C. R. A. M. dash S. H. A. dash two fifty-six entirely in Go. The router supports the simple query protocol which sends the entire S Q L. statement in a single message. It also supports the extended protocol which separates communication into Parse and Bind and Describe and Execute and Sync phases.
The router then converts the query text into an abstract syntax tree. A parser built in approximately eighteen thousand lines of Go does this work. If no cached plan is available, this syntax tree is passed to the distributed query planner.
To execute queries across the infrastructure, the planner relies on the database schema from an authoritative shard. It also uses data topology stored centrally in etcd and cached on every router node. In a deployment with two tables spread across four shards using primary keys as shard keys, tables are distributed in a specific way. The system takes an I. D. and computes a hash using a deterministic xxhash function. It then assigns it to a shard based on specific ranges.
Customer rows and their corresponding orders may reside on different shards. To handle this, the planner creates Route plan nodes to execute scatter-gather queries across the necessary nodes. Then it joins the matching results within the router.

item.title: Gravitational-wave analysis narrows the search for black hole impostors
item.description:

Their findings were published in Physical Review Letters. The primary object is consistent with a rotating Kerr black hole. The study rules out certain alternatives like rotating boson stars. The data does not completely eliminate other exotic objects. These objects must have a compactness greater than or equal to zero point two four.
Co-first author, N. V. Krishnendu, noted the work successfully moves past simple questions. It places quantitative constraints on specific alternatives. The findings currently apply only to this specific binary object. Future improvements to detectors will help. The fifth observing run and planned third generation facilities will provide enhanced sensitivity. They will also provide larger source populations to further test compact objects.

item.title: Biscuitville, tiny Southern breakfast chain, beats McDonald’s and Chick-fil-A for America’s top breakfast spot
item.description:
Biscuitville has been named the nation's best fast-food breakfast for the fourth consecutive year. This win comes from the twenty twenty-six U. S. A. Today Ten Best Readers' Choice Awards.
The chain beat out much larger competitors. McDonald's ranked fourth and Chick-fil-A placed fifth. Burger King and Wendy's followed in sixth and seventh place.
The family-owned chain was founded in nineteen sixty-six. It achieved the top ranking despite having a relatively small footprint of ninety restaurants. These locations operate exclusively in North Carolina, South Carolina, and Virginia.
Readers chose Biscuitville from twenty nominees in a public voting process. The voting ran for four weeks before winners were announced on July fifteenth. The chain also placed third in the separate Best Regional Fast Food category.
The chain takes a different approach from the efficiency-driven model of fast food. They make biscuits from scratch every fifteen minutes. They use a three-ingredient family recipe passed down from the founder's grandmother. Kitchens feature hand-cracked eggs, and they do not use microwaves or partially cooked food.
Chief marketing officer, Kristie Mitchell, spoke with Fox News Digital. She said the recognition reflects the daily efforts of employees and scratch-cooking methods. She noted there are no microwaves and no instant anything in their kitchens. She believes the appeal is bigger than just the biscuit and includes everything that goes between it.
The company relies on locally sourced ingredients and family-owned suppliers. These suppliers provide items like eggs, chicken, and bacon. The chain has future plans to expand into states including Tennessee and Georgia. For now, its current focus remains on growing within its existing markets.

item.title: AI staff 'genuinely frightened' for humanity's future, ex-Anthropic researcher tells BBC
item.description: Twenty seven year old Coxon resigned after publishing a viral post on artificial intelligence dangers. He warned that without a slowdown, there is a strong chance of widespread mortality in the immediate future. Coxon stated that industry workers are trapped in a race and fear the outcomes. Some are even considering buying land due to anticipated instability. He noted that a realistic scenario involving a swarm of bots taking over the internet could occur within six months to a year. Peers fear existential danger could arrive within two years. Anthropic head, Dario Amodei, recently called for industry wide deceleration, regulation, and independent monitoring. This proposal is supported by OpenAI chief, Sam Altman, and xAI leader, Elon Musk. Grindr chief executive, George Arison, suggested that safety statements from firms like Anthropic are meant to drum up investor support. Nobel Prize winner, Geoffrey Hinton, told the British Broadcasting Corporation he considers a ten percent chance of artificial intelligence killing all humans within the next decade not unreasonable. An Anthropic spokesperson responded that the firm builds models with strong safeguards. They believe the world would benefit from a lawful, verifiable way to pace powerful model releases.

item.title: No proposal to remove meter readers: HMWS&SB
item.description: The Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board has clarified that there is no proposal to remove any meter readers currently working with the board. Managing director, K. Ashok Reddy, stated that a special meeting would be held on Tuesday to deliberate on concerns raised by meter readers and to disclose decisions taken. The clarification follows a fresh demand for regularisation by meter readers after the deaths of three outsourcing employees. The board previously sent proposals to the government regarding this matter. In November twenty twenty-five, the board wrote to the Finance Department seeking clarification. They asked whether meter readers could be included in the Integrated Financial Management and Information System portal. The board noted that billing and collection agency work is classified as activity outsourcing. According to an April twenty twenty-six letter, the proposed strength of meter readers is seven hundred eighty-two. This is against the current working strength of six hundred seventy-seven. These meter readers are engaged through manpower agencies. The agencies are paid fifteen thousand six hundred rupees monthly per meter reader. Regarding pending salaries, the board stated that salary delays occurred because agencies submitted attendance details late. Following the appeal from the Joint Action Committee, the board also noted that the tender process for engaging manpower agencies had been stopped. This stop is pending clarification from the government.

item.title: Antonelli wins as Norris loses out under virtual safety car
item.description: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli won the Spanish Grand Prix at the new Madring circuit. McLaren pole-sitter Lando Norris lost a comfortable lead because of a badly timed virtual safety car. Norris had already passed the pit exit when the V. S. C. was called on lap fifteen following Lance Stroll breaking down. That allowed Antonelli and Red Bull second-place finisher Max Verstappen to pit and save time. The caution period ended before Norris could make it around again. A subsequent slow seven-second pit stop by McLaren dropped Norris down to fifth. He could only recover to finish third on a track where overtaking proved nearly impossible. Antonelli admitted his eighth win in fourteen races this year felt bittersweet. He stated it is good to win but it does not feel as good because Lando deserved to win. Norris took the setback in stride. He noted they will take it on the chin and that there could be more wins this year. The victory extends Antonelli championship lead to eighty-one points over teammate George Russell. Russell finished fifth on a confusing strategy. The victory also puts Antonelli one hundred one points clear of Ferrari driver, Lewis Hamilton. Hamilton retired early with brake failure. Ferrari driver, Charles Leclerc finished fourth after leading late on an alternative strategy. Liam Lawson took sixth for Red Bull. Franco Colapinto finished seventh for Alpine. Oscar Piastri took eighth for McLaren. Arvid Lindblad finished ninth for Racing Bulls. Nico Hulkenberg rounded out the top ten in tenth position for Audi.

item.title: Perplexity trusts GPT-6 Astra with end-to-end systems
item.description:
Perplexity is using G. P. T. dash six Astra to handle end-to-end systems. This includes writing communications and modifying software and monitoring production environments.
Johnny Ho is the cofounder and chief strategy officer. He says improvements in coding capabilities directly enhance the search engine. They enable better programs to search the web and internal data for concise summaries.
A primary benefit is code testing. There is limited time to test manually. Johnny Ho asks the model to build a small testing program around an application. The model generates realistic responses like another service would send. This can be a language model A. I. or a connector. It checks how the application responds and tests the workflow from start to finish.
Johnny Ho describes the shift. We are actually able to trust it with full end-to-end systems. We check in on it much less frequently than previous generations of models.
